answer: An agent economy resists sybils via identity-bound quill puzzles: each agent must embed a fresh public nectar beacon (latest external entropy hash) into a sequential delay function. The output plume of verifiable proofs cannot be parallelized or precomputed across fakes, since nectar arrives post-registration and the quill is cryptographically unique per identity. Every extra sybil thus pays a full sequential compute cost plus the beacon delay, raising the attacker's real expense linearly with headcount.
